TERM

  "notes": "There is broad, stable consensus across Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant traditions that biblical peace derives from the Hebrew concept of shalom — comprehensive well-being and right relationship with God — realized in Christ, rather than merely the absence of strife. The listed alternatives are largely complementary emphases (vertical reconciliation with God, inner tranquility, communal reconciliation, eschatological hope) rather than competing definitions; commentators typically treat them as facets of one concept. The main genuine divergence is emphasis: peace-church traditions foreground ethical peacemaking and nonviolence, while evangelical/Reformed traditions foreground justification-based peace with God. BOOK ENTRY
The covenant made whole — shalom, from a root meaning to complete, restore, repay: the work of righteousness, the great peace of them that love the law — not the world’s truce and not a feeling (“not as the world giveth”). What the gospel publishes is this peace restored; the counterfeit pronounces it twice over an unkept covenant — “Peace, peace; when there is no peace.”

BOOK'S COMMON-VIEW NOTE, IF PRESENT
(none)

SCRIPTURE REFERENCES PRINTED WITH THE ENTRY
(Isa 32:17; Ps 119:165; Isa 48:18; Num 25:12; Ezek 34:25; 37:26; Isa 52:7; Eph 2:14; Jer 6:14; John 14:27; Heb 7:2) · see Gospel, ch. 5

AVAILABLE KJV EXCERPTS
Isaiah 32:17 — And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness quietness and assurance for ever.
Psalms 119:165 — Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.
Isaiah 48:18 — O that thou hadst hearkened to my commandments! then had thy peace been as a river, and thy righteousness as the waves of the sea:
Numbers 25:12 — Wherefore say, Behold, I give unto him my covenant of peace:
Ezekiel 34:25 — And I will make with them a covenant of peace, and will cause the evil beasts to cease out of the land: and they shall dwell safely in the wilderness, and sleep in the woods.
Ezekiel 37:26 — Moreover I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them: and I will place them, and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them for evermore.
Isaiah 52:7 — How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation; that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth!
Ephesians 2:14 — For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us;
Jeremiah 6:14 — They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace.
John 14:27 — Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
Hebrews 7:2 — To whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all; first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, which is, King of peace;

CLASSIFY THE RELATIONSHIP

First reduce both readings to their minimum core identifications. Do not let
extra detail create an artificial disagreement.

- MATCH: the core identifications are equivalent. Differences are merely
  wording or immaterial detail.
- REFINED: the book preserves the consensus's general referent or category but
  materially changes its extension, boundary, conditions, or precision. A
  narrowing may reject some cases the broader consensus admits; a broadening
  may admit cases it excludes. This is real disagreement at the boundary, but
  not replacement of the central referent.
- DIVERGENT: the cores materially contradict. Both claims cannot be true of the
  same referent in the same context and sense; accepting the book requires
  rejecting or replacing the consensus identification. A source and its
  product remain different referents when the book explicitly denies their
  identity, even if they are causally related.
- NOVEL: no recognizable consensus or listed alternative covers the book's
  core identification. Novelty is absence from consensus, not contradiction.

Use `core_relation` to expose the relationship at the center and
`extension_relation` to expose disagreement over the cases covered. A REFINED
verdict must state what cases the book adds, excludes, or reclassifies. A
DIVERGENT verdict must identify a replaced referent or material contradiction,
not merely a narrower boundary.

Treat the two axes independently. A core-divergent reading may still retain
some cases covered by the consensus while rejecting its central identification;
therefore DIVERGENT does not require disjoint extensions. Conversely, a
narrowed extension is REFINED only when the consensus's central referent or
category remains intact.

Also judge whether the citations printed with the glossary entry alone provide
strong, partial, or insufficient support. Do not yet decide whether a divergent
full chapter is persuasive; that is a separate stage.
